# Executive summary

For a one-page reviewer view, see [PORTFOLIO_BRIEF.md](PORTFOLIO_BRIEF.md).

This project demonstrates a reusable manufacturing-quality workflow rather than a DED-specific model.

The real-data question is:

> **Does an in-process signal improve prediction of the final physical CTQ beyond the commanded recipe?**

On 23 evidence-clean DED-LB runs containing 4,905 laser-active IR frames, adding two simple IR features reduces grouped-held-out bead-width RMSE from **0.4683 mm to 0.4279 mm**, an **8.64% reduction**, while pooled held-out R² increases from **0.250 to 0.374**.

A harder leave-one-speed-level-out test remains below zero R², so the result is bounded to the sampled process window.

The second question is:

> **What must happen before a CTQ can drive production control?**

The public DED data do not contain a valid crossed/equivalent MSA study, production population, or engineering specification limits. The real-data path therefore stops automatically before capability and SPC.

A separate **synthetic-only production stream** demonstrates the downstream control workflow:

```text
process-to-CTQ evidence
        ↓
measurement-system qualification
        ↓
stable baseline
        ↓
capability gate
        ↓
SPC monitoring
        ↓
special-cause signal
        ↓
OCAP containment
        ↓
corrective action
        ↓
requalification required
```

The synthetic stream is not used to make claims about DED capability.

![System architecture](figures/system-architecture.svg){fig-alt="Existing CAD/PLM, CAE, machine, MES, and metrology systems normalize into a canonical engineering model feeding FEA verification and predictive quality/process control."}

# Why this architecture

Current manufacturing guidance supports a control-loop interpretation rather than treating MSA, capability, SPC, and the control plan as isolated calculations.

AIAG's 2024 standalone Control Plan manual added guidance for highly automated manufacturing, software-managed control plans, Safe Launch, and stronger reaction-plan expectations. The 2026 AIAG/VDA SPC manual explicitly connects process knowledge, statistical monitoring, capability, control-plan execution, and time-dependent behavior. NIST likewise distinguishes **control limits**, which describe process behavior, from **specification limits**, which describe product requirements.

That suggests a software workflow with explicit gates:

1. trust the measurement;
2. establish a stable baseline;
3. assess capability against engineering specifications;
4. activate monitoring;
5. react to special causes;
6. require requalification after corrective action.

The software should refuse to skip a gate.

# Canonical CTQ contract

The authoritative production object is not a chart or a Cpk number. It is the CTQ definition:

```text
CTQ
├── feature / characteristic identity
├── units
├── specification revision
├── LSL / target / USL
└── measurement-system identity
```

Everything else is a derived projection of that definition plus observed data.

This mirrors the broader project rule: authoritative engineering intent stays upstream; analyses, charts, capability indices, and reaction artifacts remain downstream and revision-bound.

# Real process-to-CTQ evidence

The open Zenodo DED-LB Ti-6Al-4V dataset includes commanded parameters, process monitoring, IR imagery, and metallographic cross sections.

The admitted dataset contains:

- tracks 28–50;
- monitoring captures C40–C62;
- 23 same-run observations;
- 4,905 laser-active IR frames;
- same-track macrograph-derived bead geometry.

The monitoring-capture IDs are not deposition-track IDs. A naive join initially generated a stronger result, but command-vs-monitor checks falsified the mapping. The admitted relation is:

[
capture = track + 12
]

for the selected source block.

# Prediction result

A fixed standardized ridge-regression treatment compares a recipe-only baseline with recipe plus two active-frame IR features.

## Primary grouped holdout

Leave one powder-flow level out at a time:

| Model | RMSE | MAE | Held-out R² |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Recipe only | 0.4683 mm | 0.3859 mm | 0.250 |
| Recipe + IR | **0.4279 mm** | **0.3391 mm** | **0.374** |

Relative RMSE reduction: **8.64%**.

**Later falsification (post-hoc, not blind):** the [full comparator study](analysis/falsification/FINDINGS.md) used train-fold-only tuning and a stronger polynomial recipe-only model. Its best recipe-only model scored **0.3868 mm RMSE**, beating the original fixed recipe-plus-IR model's 0.4279 mm on this same 23-track corpus; within-speed IR permutations gave p = 0.184. The initial 8.64% comparison is not evidence of a general IR-specific improvement or scientific novelty. The selected best recipe model was itself chosen post-hoc, and all observations remain from one source dataset.


![Real DED grouped-held-out prediction result](figures/prediction-performance.svg){fig-alt="Recipe-only bead-width RMSE of 0.4683 mm versus recipe plus IR RMSE of 0.4279 mm, with unseen-speed extrapolation explicitly unsupported."}

## Unseen-speed stress test

| Model | RMSE | MAE | Held-out R² |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Recipe only | 0.6331 mm | 0.5789 mm | -0.371 |
| Recipe + IR | 0.5925 mm | 0.5163 mm | -0.201 |

This does not establish extrapolation to new speed regimes.

# Real-data quality gate

The workflow then asks whether the same DED CTQ can proceed into MSA, capability, and SPC.

It cannot.

```text
prediction        SUPPORTED WITHIN WINDOW
MSA               NOT ASSESSABLE
capability        NOT ASSESSABLE
SPC               NOT ACTIVE
```

Reasons include:

- no crossed or equivalent measurement-system study;
- no production population;
- no engineering specification limits;
- no qualified production time series.

The engine returns these as typed gate outcomes instead of calculating meaningless indices.

# Synthetic downstream demonstration

To demonstrate the full manufacturing workflow without inventing facts about the public dataset, the repository contains a clearly marked synthetic control scenario.

## Measurement-system gate

The synthetic crossed Gage R&R fixture contains:

- 10 parts;
- 3 operators;
- 2 repeats per part/operator cell.

The ANOVA variance-component treatment returns:

- Gage R&R study variation: **3.47%**;
- percent of synthetic tolerance: **3.20%**;
- distinct categories: **40**.

Against the declared demo policy, the synthetic measurement system qualifies.

These thresholds are project-demo policy inputs, not represented as universal AIAG/customer requirements.

# Stable baseline

The synthetic production baseline contains 32 individual observations.

An I-MR treatment yields:

- center line: **9.9997 mm**;
- LCL: **9.7809 mm**;
- UCL: **10.2185 mm**;
- no declared baseline special-cause signals.

The baseline therefore qualifies for the next demo gate.

The current demo uses I-MR because the synthetic sampling structure is one measurement per produced unit. A production implementation should select the chart from the actual data type, subgroup structure, process dynamics, and monitoring objective rather than defaulting to I-MR.

# Capability

Only after MSA and baseline stability pass does the workflow calculate capability.

Synthetic demonstration:

| Metric | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Cp | 2.743 |
| Cpk | 2.741 |
| Pp | 4.016 |
| Ppk | 4.014 |

Again, these numbers describe only the synthetic workflow fixture.

The important software behavior is that capability becomes **not assessable** when MSA, stability, population size, or engineering specifications are absent.

# SPC before spec failure

The synthetic monitor stream introduces a deliberate upward process shift.

The first alarm occurs at:

**10.26 mm**

The synthetic UCL is:

**10.2185 mm**

The engineering USL is:

**10.6 mm**

Therefore the process is statistically out of control while the measured unit is still within engineering specification.

This is the reason the workflow keeps control limits and specification limits as separate objects.

A simple pass/fail inspection would still call the 10.26 mm unit acceptable. The process-control layer sees evidence of a special cause and invokes the reaction plan earlier.

![Synthetic SPC signal occurs before specification failure](figures/spc-ocap.svg){fig-alt="Synthetic control chart showing a first special-cause signal at 10.26 mm above the UCL but still below the 10.6 mm USL, followed by OCAP containment and required requalification."}

# OCAP lifecycle

This is where XState is justified.

The runtime lifecycle is:

```text
unqualified
→ measurementQualified
→ baselineStable
→ capabilityQualified
→ controlActive
→ outOfControl
→ containment
→ requalificationRequired
```

The synthetic reaction plan requires:

- identify and quarantine product since the last known-good control point;
- preserve run, lot, tool, and measurement provenance;
- stop the synthetic process on a confirmed special-cause signal;
- investigate and correct the assignable cause;
- verify the measurement system remains qualified;
- collect a fresh stable baseline;
- reassess capability before normal control resumes.

The system deliberately does **not** jump directly from correction back to production.

# Why Effect and XState are separated

The project uses the tools for different jobs.

**Effect** orchestrates analytical gates and fails closed when required evidence is missing.

**XState** models the event-driven operational lifecycle after the statistical gates have established that control is eligible.

The equations remain pure TypeScript functions. The state machine does not own statistical truth, and the statistical functions do not secretly change operational state.

# Generated control plan

Once the synthetic measurement system, baseline, and capability qualify, the engine generates a revision-bound control-plan object containing:

- CTQ identity;
- specification revision;
- measurement-system identity;
- LSL / target / USL;
- I-MR center line and control limits;
- sampling instruction;
- named reaction-plan owner;
- containment, stop, restore-control, and requalification actions.

This avoids maintaining a second hand-entered definition of the CTQ inside the control plan.

# Reusability

The workflow is intentionally process-agnostic:

```text
process
→ signal
→ CTQ
→ measurement qualification
→ stability
→ capability
→ control
→ reaction
```

For another industry, the inputs change:

- welding: current/vision/thermal signal → weld CTQ;
- battery assembly: force/vision data → dimensional/electrical CTQ;
- semiconductor: tool/metrology data → thickness/uniformity/defect CTQ;
- consumer electronics: assembly/metrology data → gap/flush/dimensional CTQ;
- machining: tool/process data → dimension/surface CTQ.

The gate semantics do not need to change.


# Day-one integration boundaries

The reusable quality workflow is deliberately separated from transport and vendor details. External systems are normalized into canonical product, process, measurement, genealogy, and solver-result identities before any FEA or quality calculation is allowed to consume them.

```text
CAD / PLM        CAE             machine / edge        MES             metrology
STEP AP242       CalculiX         OPC UA                REST/SQL        QIF 3.x
                 Nastran          MTConnect
                                  Sparkplug B
     \              |                |                  |                 /
      \             |                |                  |                /
       +-------------+----------------+------------------+---------------+
                                      |
                                      v
                         canonical engineering model
                         product revision / feature
                         unit / run / recipe genealogy
                         process signal / measurement
                         normalized structural result
                                      |
                              +-------+-------+
                              |               |
                              v               v
                        FEA verification   MSA / capability /
                                           SPC / OCAP
```

## Implemented protocol semantics

**STEP Part 21 / AP242.** The adapter checks the Part 21 exchange envelope, HEADER/DATA sections, `FILE_SCHEMA`, `FILE_NAME`, and extracts product/revision identity from the recorded fixture. It intentionally stops before geometry-kernel semantics. AP242 is the upstream product-definition boundary; the project does not claim to implement AP242 as a whole.

**QIF 3.x.** The adapter validates the QIF 3 namespace/version and maps characteristic-measurement identity, actual component, measurement-device reference, timestamp, status, numeric value, unit, and combined uncertainty into the canonical measurement object. It is an evidence extractor, not a replacement for a full QIF XSD validator.

**OPC UA.** The canonical node reference stores the namespace URI plus identifier. The current session `NamespaceArray` is used to derive the transport NodeId because namespace indexes are server/session-local. DataValues with Bad StatusCode are rejected and process signals require a source timestamp.

**MTConnect 2.5.** The adapter handles `probe`, `current`, and `sample` response shapes, records `instanceId`, and advances the recorded `nextSequence` cursor. A changed Agent `instanceId` fails closed and requires cursor reinitialization.

**Sparkplug B 3.0.** The adapter validates the `spBv1.0/<group>/<message>/<edge>/<device?>` topic structure, requires NBIRTH before data, requires DBIRTH before device data, checks the NBIRTH `bdSeq` and `Node Control/Rebirth` metrics, and enforces Edge Node sequence continuity modulo 256.

**MES genealogy.** MES is treated as a business-system boundary rather than a pretend universal protocol. Recorded, REST-style, and parameterized SQL adapters resolve the same canonical unit → run → recipe revision → equipment genealogy.

**CAE.** Existing project-executed CalculiX results and a recorded Nastran BDF/F06 compatibility fixture both normalize into the same structural-result contract. The Nastran lane currently admits nodal displacement only; unsupported quantities stay null rather than being fabricated.

## Adapter claim boundary

The adapter suite demonstrates that the internal engineering model is not coupled to demo files or one vendor. It does **not** claim:

- AP242 geometry-kernel completeness;
- full QIF schema validation;
- OPC UA server certification;
- MTConnect Agent certification;
- Sparkplug TCK compatibility;
- live MES vendor certification;
- live Nastran/ANSYS/Abaqus execution.

Those require real endpoint/software qualification. The portfolio claim is narrower: the protocols are represented at the correct integration boundaries and their critical identity/state semantics are tested.

# Standards-informed boundaries

The design references:

- AIAG MSA 4th Edition overview;
- AIAG Control Plan 1st Edition;
- AIAG & VDA SPC Manual 1st Edition, published July 2026;
- NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook sections on stability, capability, and control charts.

The implementation does not reproduce proprietary manual content and does not claim that the synthetic policy thresholds are mandated by those standards.

# Supporting evidence

The NIST AMB2022-01 CMM case remains the uncertainty-aware physical-metrology example.

The synthetic structural fixture, Gmsh/CalculiX refinement study, and independent Julia implementation remain a numerical-verification appendix.

They support the engineering-method story without competing with the manufacturing-quality headline.
